notes: Summary: mid-market knowledge platform for customer success + in-app help. Looking to replace ad-hoc search with semantic layer (embeddings + FAISS/Pinecone currently).
Initial ask: embeddings quality parity with current pipeline, predictable throughput for search (sub-150ms median for 1-2K concurrent search qps), and cheaper unit token cost for nightly re-embeds.
Customer quote: 'We need consistent tail latency — spikes kill UX for live search and conversational bots.'
Current infra: nightly Spark job writes embeddings to S3, ingests to Pinecone. ~5M docs once/day re-embed, plus realtime user uploads (~10-20K/day).
Throughput targets: 200 qps embedding ingest for batch window, 800 qps read for search during business hours (parallel requests from product).
Cost sensitivity: mid-market buyer, tight unit economics; wants a clear cost comparison Hosted vs Dedicated including reserved blocks + burst pricing.
Security: requires SSO / SAML, SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. Data residency requirement: primary US, possibility EU later.
Integration: expects a connector to S3 + native hooks for their vector DB (currently Pinecone) or migration path. Also wants a simple Spark connector for batch re-embed job.
Observed technical concerns: KV cache behavior for conversational re-rank, model quantization impact on recall@10, and autoscaling warm-up time for Dedicated pools.
Competitive notes: evaluated OpenAI embeddings (quality ok, cost higher), tested Pinecone for vector store but wants tighter operational coupling (Redwood offering + routing looks attractive).
Pricing convo: asked for committed capacity discount tiers and an example cost model for 5M doc nightlies + steady-state search traffic.
Sales tactic: PLG self-serve path tested by their devs — they spun up hosted keys, ran a quick embeddings pass on 50k docs, liked latency and API ergonomics.
